title: Rate-window observations & repro notes
content:
Objective:
- Quick scratchpad for the weird 401/429 behavior observed from the macOS CLI clients and one internal node pool (eu-west-1b). Trying to capture commands, timing, headers, and hypotheses so we can hand this to SRE/Runtime.

High-level summary (so I don't forget):
- Multiple short bursts (~20 reqs/sec for ~10s) against hosted API with same API key produce 429s in a way that doesn't line up with quota headers.
- Sometimes we get 401s in the same incident window for the same key — looks like auth check failed intermittently (not a full revocation).
- Retry-After header present on some 429s (value 3 or 60) and missing on others.
- Observed difference between sequential single-thread curl and parallel python requests.

Environment/clients tested:
- macOS 14 laptop, curl 8.4
- small k8s job (node-pool: eu-west-1b) using python-requests pool (concurrent.futures ThreadPoolExecutor)
- internal traffic generator (go), single connection reusing keep-alive

Commands I ran (repro attempts) — timestamps in UTC:
1) Baseline single request (ok):
   $ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REW_KEY_REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt": "hi","max_tokens": 10}'
   -> 200 OK
   Response headers (partial):
     x-rate-limit-limit: 600
     x-rate-limit-remaining: 599
     x-rate-limit-window: 60

2) Small burst sequential (succeeds):
   for i in {1..5}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer REW_KEY_REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":1}'; done
   -> 200 200 200 200 200

3) Parallel burst from laptop (problematic):
   # python snippet -> fire 100 requests in ~8s across 10 threads
   -> results: 68x 200, 32x 429
   Example 429 response headers from one of them:
     HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
     Retry-After: 3
     x-rate-limit-limit: 600
     x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
     x-rate-limit-reset: 2024-11-08T18:23:40Z

4) Back-to-back repeated parallel run (different behavior):
   -> results: 45x 200, 40x 429, 15x 401
   Example 401 snippet:
     HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
     x-error-code: api_key_invalid_signature
     x-request-id: rwd-8f3b2a
     body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"signature mismatch"}

5) Key rotate test (same key vs new key):
   - Generated a fresh key from Console for test-key-02. Sent same burst -> mostly 200s, ~2x 429s.
   - Re-used old key concurrently in same window -> old key produced 401s and occasional 429s.

Observations / patterns:
- 429s correlate with concurrency and burstiness, but 401s correlate with the older key being used concurrently with the new key (same account).
- Some 429 responses show x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 and a reset timestamp; others omit remaining header entirely.
- Retry-After values vary — small values (3s) when we triggered a short burst backoff path; 60s when the backend enforcement switched to a longer penalty window.
- 401 error bodies show different x-error-code values. api_key_expired vs api_key_invalid_signature. The latter suggests the signature layer intermittently failed (possible HSM/KMS auth flap?).
- Node-pool traffic using persistent HTTP/1.1 connections saw fewer 401s but still 429s; suggesting per-connection vs per-key attribution differences.

Server-side traces I asked for (tickets):
- INFRA-784: asked runtime team to attach trace for request ids rwd-8f3b2a, rwd-8f3b2b, rwd-8f3b2c. Waiting for spans to confirm whether auth check preceded rate check.

Hypotheses (ordered by my confidence):
1) Sliding vs fixed window mismatch between enforcement and header calc: enforcement is doing a per-second bucketed count that can spike while header reflects a longer averaging window -> 429s look sudden. (medium confidence)
2) Race in key lookup/rotation service: rotating key created transient signature validation failures when two keys were used very close in time because cache invalidation lag. (high confidence for the 401s)
3) Upstream proxy (edge LB) applying different rate policies per connection vs per API key, so keep-alive reuse changes behavior. (medium)
4) Some internal fallback path setting longer Retry-After when a higher-tier enforcement is engaged (e.g., global throttle after regional overload). (low)

What I tried to further probe:
- Serial vs parallel: confirmed parallel increases 429 rate dramatically.
- Connection reuse vs new connections: reusing same curl connection (keep-alive) produced slightly lower 429 ratio.
- Short sleeps between threads (staggering starts) reduced 429s -> supports burst sensitivity theory.
- Deliberate header mutation: tried removing x-client-id header (we sometimes set one) -> no difference.

Immediate next steps (recommended):
- Ask runtime to confirm whether auth and rate-limit checks are sequential or parallel; need trace of order for the sample request-ids.
- Ask infra to check KMS/HSM logs for key signature failures on the exact timestamps (matching 401s).
- Re-run a controlled experiment from a single VM with traffic generator that can control concurrency and inter-arrival times (I can run this if SRE gives greenlight).
- If sliding-window enforcement is present, request that header calculation be aligned with enforcement or add header explanation (e.g., x-rate-limit-window-type: sliding|fixed).

Notes-to-self (quick checklist):
- [ ] Capture full tcpdump for next repro (include TLS handshake times).
- [ ] Run a client that creates 1 TCP connection and multiplexes 1k small requests with configurable inter-arrival to map out envelope.
- [ ] Add debug logging on client side: timestamp, pid, thread-id, connection-id, req-id returned by server.

Random thrown-in examples I saved while debugging (raw):
- 429 case without Retry-After:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  x-rate-limit-limit: 600
  x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
  x-request-id: rwd-9c4a1f
  body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"try again later"}

- 401 case with mismatch:
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  x-error-code: api_key_invalid_signature
  x-request-id: rwd-8f3b2a
  body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"signature mismatch (kid=key-old-3)"}

If someone from runtime or infra picks this up:
- Please prioritize: 1) traces for request ids above, 2) KMS/HSM signature logs for the minute windows 2024-11-08T18:22:00Z - 2024-11-08T18:25:00Z, 3) confirmation on whether headers are calculated from the enforcement bucket or an aggregation cache.

Timestamped breadcrumbs (UTC):
- 2024-11-08T18:20:05Z: started baseline checks
- 2024-11-08T18:21:10Z: first parallel run, 429s seen
- 2024-11-08T18:22:40Z: 401s start appearing (key-old-3 showing invalid_signature)
- 2024-11-08T18:23:50Z: generated key-new-7 and re-ran -> improvement for that key

End of notes. Will convert to a more formal handoff if SRE asks for it.
